title: 1 Corinthians Chapter 5 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 1 Corinthians chapter 5 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 1 Corinthians Chapter 5 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 1 Corinthians Chapter 5.

questions.question: In 1 Corinthians 5, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: my spirit, with the power of our Lord Jesus Christ
deliver such an one unto Satan
questions.explanation: The mention of fornication is the first event recorded in the chapter, as stated in 1 Corinthians 5:1.

questions.question: What is reported among the Corinthians in 1 Corinthians 5?
options: that one should have his father's wife
questions.correctAnswer: that one should have his father's wife
questions.explanation: This is directly stated in 1 Corinthians 5:1, where it is reported that there is fornication among them.

questions.question: How did the Corinthians respond to the fornication mentioned?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 5:2 indicates that the Corinthians were puffed up rather than mourning over the sin.

questions.question: What did Paul judge concerning the man who committed fornication?
questions.explanation: According to 1 Corinthians 5:2, Paul expressed that the man who committed the deed should be taken away from among them.

questions.question: In whose name did Paul instruct the Corinthians to act regarding the fornicator?
options: in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ
in the name of the apostles
questions.correctAnswer: in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ
questions.explanation: Paul specifically states in 1 Corinthians 5:4 that they should act in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ.

questions.question: What is the purpose of delivering the fornicator to Satan according to Paul?
options: to expose him to the world
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 5:5 indicates that the purpose of delivering such a person to Satan is so that the spirit may be saved in the day of the Lord Jesus.

questions.question: What did Paul claim about his presence in relation to the Corinthians?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 5:3 states that Paul is absent in body but present in spirit.

questions.question: What emotional state did Paul expect the Corinthians to have regarding the fornicator's action?
questions.explanation: Paul expected them to mourn over the sin, as indicated in 1 Corinthians 5:2.

questions.question: What power does Paul refer to when addressing the Corinthians' actions?
options: the power of our Lord Jesus Christ
questions.correctAnswer: the power of our Lord Jesus Christ
questions.explanation: Paul mentions the power of our Lord Jesus Christ in 1 Corinthians 5:4 when instructing them on how to act.

questions.question: What type of immorality is specifically mentioned in 1 Corinthians 5?
questions.explanation: Fornication is specifically mentioned in 1 Corinthians 5:1 as the type of immorality reported among the Corinthians.

questions.question: What should happen to the man who committed fornication according to Paul?
questions.explanation: Paul states in 1 Corinthians 5:2 that the one who committed this deed should be taken away from among them.

questions.question: True or False: Paul was physically present with the Corinthians.
questions.explanation: Paul states in 1 Corinthians 5:3 that he is absent in body.

questions.question: True or False: The fornication mentioned was not known among the Gentiles.
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 5:1 indicates that the fornication reported was not even named among the Gentiles.

questions.question: True or False: Paul encouraged the Corinthians to ignore the fornicator's actions.
questions.explanation: Paul does not encourage ignoring the actions; instead, he wants them to take action against the fornicator as stated in 1 Corinthians 5:2.

questions.question: True or False: Paul said to deliver the fornicator to the church.
questions.explanation: Paul instructs to deliver the fornicator to Satan, not to the church, as stated in 1 Corinthians 5:5.

medium.title: 1 Corinthians Chapter 5 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 1 Corinthians Chapter 5 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What does Paul say about glorying in 1 Corinthians 5:6?
options: It is a sign of faith.
questions.explanation: This is correct as stated in 1 Corinthians 5:6, emphasizing that such pride is detrimental.

questions.question: What will happen if you purge out the old leaven according to 1 Corinthians 5:7?
options: You will be a new lump.
questions.correctAnswer: You will be a new lump.
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 5:7 indicates that purging the old leaven leads to becoming a new lump, symbolizing renewal.

questions.question: What is the purpose of keeping the feast as mentioned in 1 Corinthians 5:8?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 5:8 instructs believers to keep the feast with unleavened bread of sincerity and truth, contrasting with malice.

questions.question: What does 1 Corinthians 5:9 instruct regarding fornicators?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 5:9 expresses that Paul had previously written not to associate with fornicators, emphasizing the need for discipline.

questions.question: According to 1 Corinthians 5:10, who are believers not to avoid completely?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 5:10 clarifies that Paul does not mean to avoid all sinners, but specifically those within the church who live in sin.

questions.question: Why does Paul mention the need to purge out old leaven?
questions.explanation: Purge the old leaven as stated in 1 Corinthians 5:7 is about ensuring the church remains pure and united in Christ.

questions.question: What does the term 'leaven' symbolize in 1 Corinthians 5:6-8?
questions.explanation: In these verses, leaven represents sinful influences that can permeate and corrupt the whole community.

questions.question: In 1 Corinthians 5:5, what is the aim of delivering someone to Satan?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 5:5 indicates that the purpose is the destruction of the flesh, so that the spirit may be saved, highlighting restoration.

questions.question: What attitude should believers have toward sin in their midst according to 1 Corinthians 5:2?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 5:2 points out that the church was puffed up instead of mourning over the sin present among them.

questions.question: What should believers avoid according to 1 Corinthians 5:8?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 5:8 states that believers should keep the feast without the old leaven or the leaven of malice and wickedness.

questions.question: What is the significance of Christ being referred to as our Passover in 1 Corinthians 5:7?
options: He is a sacrifice for sin.
He is a leader of the feast.
He is a symbol of joy.
He is an example of leadership.
questions.correctAnswer: He is a sacrifice for sin.
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 5:7 explains that Christ our Passover has been sacrificed for us, linking His sacrifice to the concept of purification.

questions.question: Should Christians isolate themselves from all sinners according to 1 Corinthians 5:10?
options: No, they must engage with the world.
questions.correctAnswer: No, they must engage with the world.
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 5:10 clarifies that Paul does not instruct to completely separate from sinners in the world, as that would be impossible.

questions.question: True or False: Paul encourages the Corinthians to celebrate their tolerance of sin.
questions.explanation: This is false as Paul condemns their pride and calls for mourning over sin in 1 Corinthians 5:2.

questions.question: True or False: A little leaven can affect the whole lump according to 1 Corinthians 5:6.
questions.explanation: This is true as 1 Corinthians 5:6 illustrates how a small amount of leaven can corrupt the entire community.

questions.question: True or False: Paul believes that all fornicators should be embraced within the church community.
questions.explanation: This is false as Paul instructs not to company with fornicators in 1 Corinthians 5:9.

hard.title: 1 Corinthians Chapter 5 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 1 Corinthians Chapter 5.

questions.question: According to 1 Corinthians 5:11, with which type of person are believers instructed not to eat?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 5:11 explicitly states not to eat with 'any man that is called a brother be a fornicator...'

questions.question: In 1 Corinthians 5:11, which of the following is NOT listed as a reason to avoid keeping company with a brother?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 5:11 lists 'fornicator, covetous, idolater, railer (slanderer), drunkard, extortioner' but does not mention 'prophet'.

questions.question: What rationale does Paul give in 1 Corinthians 5:12 for judging those within the church?
options: Do ye not judge them that are within?
questions.correctAnswer: Do ye not judge them that are within?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 5:12 asks rhetorically, 'do not ye judge them that are within?'

questions.question: According to 1 Corinthians 5:13, who judges 'them that are without'?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 5:13 clearly states, 'But them that are without God judgeth.'

questions.question: What action does Paul command in 1 Corinthians 5:13 regarding the wicked person among the church?
options: Put away from among yourselves that wicked person
Ignore the sin to avoid division
questions.correctAnswer: Put away from among yourselves that wicked person
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 5:13 commands, 'Therefore put away from among yourselves that wicked person.'

questions.question: In 1 Corinthians 5:11, what is the meaning of the Greek word translated as 'railer'?
options: One who speaks abusively or insults
questions.correctAnswer: One who speaks abusively or insults
questions.explanation: The Greek word 'loidoros' translated 'railer' means one who verbally abuses or insults, as seen in 1 Corinthians 5:11.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in 1 Corinthians 5:6 where Paul says, 'a little leaven leaveneth the whole lump'?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 5:6 uses 'leaven' metaphorically to signify how a small sin affects the entire community.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage is thematically connected to the call for purity and putting away sin in 1 Corinthians 5:7-8?
options: Psalm 23 - The Lord is my Shepherd
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 5:7-8 references Christ as our Passover and the call to keep the feast with unleavened bread, connecting to Exodus 12:15's instructions about unleavened bread.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the disciplinary theme of 1 Corinthians 5:5, where Paul speaks of delivering a sinner to Satan for the destruction of the flesh?
questions.explanation: Matthew 18:15-17 describes steps for church discipline, paralleling Paul's instructions in 1 Corinthians 5:5 about removing the sinner for restoration.

questions.question: What verse precedes 1 Corinthians 5:11 and discusses not keeping company with fornicators of the world?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 5:10 precedes verse 11 and instructs not to company with fornicators of the world, setting up the stronger instruction in verse 11.

questions.question: What is the Greek term for 'fornicator' used in 1 Corinthians 5:11, and what is its literal meaning?
questions.explanation: 'Porneia' is the Greek word translated as 'fornicator' in 1 Corinthians 5:11, meaning illicit sexual intercourse.

questions.question: How does 1 Corinthians 5:5 illustrate the typology of Christ’s sacrifice in relation to church discipline?
options: Delivering a sinner to Satan parallels Christ’s sacrifice for spiritual restoration
It compares the sinner to the Passover lamb
It uses the image of the temple veil tearing
It refers to Moses delivering the law
questions.correctAnswer: Delivering a sinner to Satan parallels Christ’s sacrifice for spiritual restoration
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 5:5 shows church discipline as a redemptive act aligned with Christ’s sacrifice, aiming for the spirit to be saved.

questions.question: What cultural context underpins Paul’s instruction in 1 Corinthians 5:1 about the sexual immorality involving a man and his father's wife?
options: It was considered incest and highly taboo even among Gentiles
It was a common and accepted practice
It was a Roman legal requirement
It was a ritual of the pagan religions
questions.correctAnswer: It was considered incest and highly taboo even among Gentiles
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 5:1 highlights the scandalous nature of the sin, noting it was not even named among Gentiles, indicating strong cultural taboo.

questions.question: True or False: According to 1 Corinthians 5:12, Paul asserts that believers should also judge those outside the church community.
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 5:12 states Paul has no responsibility to judge those outside, but calls for judgment of those within the church.

questions.question: True or False: 1 Corinthians 5:6 uses the image of leaven to warn that a small amount of sin can affect the entire church.
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 5:6 says, 'a little leaven leaveneth the whole lump,' metaphorically warning how sin affects the whole community.

theological.title: 1 Corinthians Chapter 5 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 1 Corinthians Chapter 5 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does 1 Corinthians 5:5 teach about salvation?
options: Salvation involves restoration through disciplinary judgment
Salvation is guaranteed regardless of behavior
Salvation is only through external rituals
questions.correctAnswer: Salvation involves restoration through disciplinary judgment
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 5:5 shows that delivering a sinner to Satan is for the destruction of the flesh so that the spirit may be saved, indicating salvation includes restoration through discipline.

questions.question: What doctrine does 1 Corinthians 5:7 teach about sanctification?
options: Believers must purge sin to become a new creation in Christ
Christ's sacrifice is unrelated to sanctification
Sanctification is achieved by legalistic observance
questions.correctAnswer: Believers must purge sin to become a new creation in Christ
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 5:7 commands believers to purge the old leaven to be a new lump, symbolizing sanctification through Christ's sacrifice.

questions.question: What doctrine about church discipline does 1 Corinthians 5:13 teach?
options: The church must expel unrepentant sinners from fellowship
The church should tolerate all sinners within
Judgment of sinners is reserved only for secular authorities
The church should never judge its members
questions.correctAnswer: The church must expel unrepentant sinners from fellowship
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 5:13 instructs the church to put away the wicked person from among themselves, indicating the necessity of church discipline.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 1 Corinthians 5:5 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 5:5 shows God's holiness in that He requires separation from sin for restoration and preservation of the spirit.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 1 Corinthians 5:13 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 5:13 reveals God's justice as He judges those outside the church and commands the church to remove wickedness within.

questions.question: How does 1 Corinthians 5 connect to the broader biblical theme of covenant purity?
options: It calls the church to maintain holiness as God’s covenant people
It abolishes the need for moral purity in the church
It focuses only on social acceptance without covenant implications
It teaches that purity is irrelevant under the New Covenant
questions.correctAnswer: It calls the church to maintain holiness as God’s covenant people
questions.explanation: The chapter’s command to purge sin connects with Old Testament covenant calls for purity (cf. Leviticus 18), showing continuity in God's people maintaining holiness.

questions.question: How does 1 Corinthians 5 prepare the church for understanding Christ's role as Passover Lamb?
options: By linking moral purity to the sacrifice of Christ as Passover
By denying any connection between Christ and Jewish festivals
By suggesting Christ's death nullifies ethical living
By emphasizing human effort over divine sacrifice
questions.correctAnswer: By linking moral purity to the sacrifice of Christ as Passover
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 5:7 explicitly identifies Christ as our Passover sacrificed for us, underscoring the theological connection between His sacrifice and moral purity.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 6 and 7 teach about the effect of sin in the church?
options: Sin corrupts the whole community and must be removed for renewal
Sin only affects the individual and need not be addressed corporately
Sin is a minor issue that Christians should ignore
Sin is tolerated to preserve unity at any cost
questions.correctAnswer: Sin corrupts the whole community and must be removed for renewal
questions.explanation: Verses 6 and 7 use the leaven metaphor to show how sin spreads through the whole assembly, so removing it results in a new, purified community.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 9 and 11 teach about association with sinners inside and outside the church?
options: Believers must separate from sinful brothers but may associate with nonbelievers
Believers must avoid all people regardless of faith
Believers should not judge anyone, inside or outside the church
Believers must isolate themselves completely from the world
questions.correctAnswer: Believers must separate from sinful brothers but may associate with nonbelievers
questions.explanation: Verses 9 and 11 distinguish between not associating with immoral believers yet allowing contact with sinful people outside the church.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 2 and 12 teach about the responsibility of the church towards internal sin versus external sin?
options: The church must judge and discipline members but not outsiders
The church should judge outsiders more harshly than insiders
The church has no role in judging anyone
The church must ignore internal sin to be welcoming
questions.correctAnswer: The church must judge and discipline members but not outsiders
questions.explanation: Verse 2 rebukes the church for pride instead of mourning sin among them; verse 12 clarifies that judging is for those inside the church, not outsiders.

questions.question: Sceptics claim 1 Corinthians 5:1-5 teaches Christians should harshly punish sinners with permanent exclusion. What does 1 Corinthians 5:1-5 actually teach?
options: Discipline aims at restoration and salvation, not permanent exclusion
Sinners must be permanently expelled with no hope of return
The passage promotes cruelty without spiritual purpose
Discipline is unnecessary because all sin is forgiven automatically
questions.correctAnswer: Discipline aims at restoration and salvation, not permanent exclusion
questions.explanation: Verses 1-5 show that delivering the sinner to Satan is for destruction of the flesh so that the spirit may be saved, indicating restorative discipline rather than permanent exclusion.

questions.question: What doctrine does 1 Corinthians 5:8 teach about Christian living in contrast to the Old Testament?
options: Christians live in sincerity and truth, not under old sinful patterns
Christians must continue old leavened traditions
Christian living removes the need for moral sincerity
The old law is entirely abolished with no ethical continuity
questions.correctAnswer: Christians live in sincerity and truth, not under old sinful patterns
questions.explanation: Verse 8 contrasts the 'old leaven' of malice and wickedness with unleavened bread of sincerity and truth, symbolizing new ethical life in Christ.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is demonstrated in 1 Corinthians 5:3 by Paul's role in church discipline?
questions.explanation: Paul states in verse 3 that though absent in body, he is present in spirit and has already judged the offender, showing his spiritual presence and authority.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 4 and 5 teach about the power of Christ in church discipline?
options: Discipline is exercised in the name and power of Christ
Discipline is a human authority independent of Christ
Discipline is a worldly practice unrelated to the church
questions.correctAnswer: Discipline is exercised in the name and power of Christ
questions.explanation: Verses 4 and 5 show that discipline is exercised when the church is gathered in the name and power of the Lord Jesus Christ, emphasizing Christ's authority.

questions.question: How does 1 Corinthians 5:10-11 contribute to the understanding of holiness and fellowship within the church?
options: Believers must avoid close fellowship with immoral believers but may associate with the ungodly in the world
Believers should avoid all contact with immoral people both inside and outside the church
Believers are called to fully embrace all sinners without distinction
Holiness is not relevant to church fellowship
questions.correctAnswer: Believers must avoid close fellowship with immoral believers but may associate with the ungodly in the world
questions.explanation: Verses 10-11 clarify that while believers should not keep company with immoral brothers, they are not to avoid all sinners in the world, maintaining a balance between holiness and mission.
